headlines.title: Cramer warns SanDisk and Western Digital are worst stocks if data center capacity shrinks
headlines.summary: Jim Cramer called out two storage giants sitting on massive year-to-date gains as the most dangerous stocks to own if one key spending trend reverses, and the math behind their profits makes the risk easy to underestimate.

headlines.title: Sandisk (SNDK)  vs. Texas Instruments (TXN): How Much Cash-Yield Protection Does Memory Offer?
headlines.summary: Our 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade includes both memory and analog exposure. Sandisk’s strong cash generation creates an apparent valuation advantage over Texas Instruments. The useful question is how much that cash can decline before the advantage disappears, rather than assuming today’s memory economics last a decade.

headlines.title: Sandisk, Datadog, Amazon Lead S&P 500 As AI Stocks Rebound
headlines.summary: Western Digital, Sandisk, Datadog, Twilio and Amazon led the S&P 500 index in Monday's stock market trading as artificial intelligence plays rebounded. Western Digital (WDC) gained 6.1% to 352.21 on Monday, still below all its key moving averages. Western Digital stock plunged 16.4% last week.

headlines.title: Last Week’s Stock Market Losers Are Bouncing Back—With CoreWeave an Exception
headlines.summary: Sandisk and Lumentum recover some ground Monday, while CoreWeave falls despite a Goldman Sachs upgrade as AI financing concerns linger.

headlines.title: Micron (MU) vs. Sandisk (SNDK): Is the Smaller Factory Bill Really an Advantage?
headlines.summary: Our 10 Best Semiconductor Stocks to Buy for the Next Decade shows where Micron and Sandisk rank against other durable chip franchises using weighted hedge-fund sentiment, durability, financial resilience and valuation. Their capital-spending lines, however, conceal different funding burdens. Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) owns substantial manufacturing capacity.

description: Sandisk Corporation develops, manufactures, and sells data storage devices and solutions using NAND flash technology in the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia, and internationally. The company provides solid state drives for desktop and notebook PCs, gaming consoles, and set top boxes; and flash-based embedded storage products for mobile phones, tablets, notebook PCs and other portable and wearable devices, automotive applications, Internet of Things, industrial, and connected home applications, as well as removable cards, universal serial bus drives, and wafers and components. It sells its products to computer manufacturers and original equipment manufacturers, datacenters, private cloud customers, cloud service providers, resellers, distributors, and retailers through its sales personnel, dealers, distributors, retailers, and subsidiaries. Sandisk Corporation was incorporated in 2024 and is based in Milpitas, California.
